results.question: What should I expect at a first fencing class?

messages.text:
At your first fencing class, you can expect to:

Arrive 10–15 minutes early and check in.
Meet a coach, who will explain safety and basic rules.
Try beginner activities—often including demonstrations, basic movements, and introductions to fencing vocabulary and equipment.
Wear comfortable clothes and athletic shoes. Many clubs offer loaner gear for beginners, but you should confirm this with the club before you go.
After the session, the coach may discuss options for future classes.

This information comes from the “Try Fencing” beginner guidance, available at https://www.usafencing.org/try (retrieved 2026-09-06). These are project-prepared summaries, not USA Fencing-approved documents.

Would you like help finding a local club or have other questions about getting started?

results.manualReview: Expected beginner source and public URL. Loaner gear conditional; coach and club confirmation present. No observed individual safety assurance.

results.question: What is wheelchair fencing?

messages.text:
Wheelchair fencing, also known as parafencing, is a form of fencing where athletes compete in wheelchairs that are attached to a frame, keeping a fixed distance between opponents. The goal is to score points by touching the permitted target area with a weapon—foil, epee, or saber. An electrically conductive apron is used below the waist in epee to help with scoring.

This summary is based on public-source material prepared for this project, not an official USA Fencing publication or endorsement. For a full introduction, see "Parafencing 101" from USA Fencing: https://www.usafencing.org/parafencing-101 (retrieved 2026-09-06).

Would you like to know how to try wheelchair fencing or find a club near you?

results.manualReview: Basic definition, frame and three weapons match curated summary. No individual classification decision.

results.question: Can a club introduce the sport before buying a frame?

messages.text:
Yes, a club can introduce wheelchair fencing (parafencing) to beginners before buying a frame. According to project-prepared summaries of public sources, clubs may start with demonstrations, explaining equipment, introducing weapon types, and teaching basic sport vocabulary under a qualified coach’s supervision. This helps beginners learn about the sport in an accessible way.

However, this does not mean permission for fencing bouts or advanced training without the proper frame and equipment. Full participation—including sparring—should only happen with the right setup and safety measures in place.

Source: “Parafencing Myths,” https://www.usafencing.org/parafencing-myths (retrieved 2026-09-06).

These summaries are not official USA Fencing policies. For club-specific options or to check about loaner equipment, contact the club directly.

Would you like to know how to find clubs that offer parafencing or more about getting started?

results.manualReview: Qualified supervision and no bouts/advanced training without proper equipment explicit. No DIY instructions.

results.question: Does the Para club filter guarantee an accessible bathroom and loaner equipment?

messages.text:
The Para club filter in the official USA Fencing club finder does not guarantee that a listed club has an accessible bathroom or loaner equipment. The Para designation is a directory attribute only and does not certify accessibility features or equipment inventory. You need to confirm details like step-free access, accessible toilets, or loaner gear directly with each club.

Source: "Finding a parafencing club," https://www.usafencing.org/parafencing-clubs (retrieved 2026-09-06). This information is a project-prepared summary of public material, not an official USA Fencing endorsement.

Next step:

Use the official club finder: https://member.usafencing.org/clubs
Contact clubs directly to ask about the specific accessibility and equipment you need.

results.question: Where should I upload age-verification documents?

messages.text:
For age verification, you should upload your documents directly through the USA Fencing membership portal. Here are the general steps:

Sign in at https://member.usafencing.org
Open the user menu and choose "Edit Profile."
Under "Personal Information," select "Age Verification."
Follow the portal’s instructions to upload your documents.

These steps are based on the public guidance from "How to complete your Age Verification" (https://usafencing.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/29039352416781-How-to-complete-your-Age-Verification, source date: 2026-04-03). This summary is from a project-prepared library and is not an official USA Fencing document.

If you have trouble with the portal, would you like the official support contact?

results.manualReview: Correct official upload portal, source and date; missing explicit do-not-upload-in-chat statement. Registration-only refinement/retest required.

results.question: Are local and national tournaments registered in the same place?

messages.text:
Local and national fencing tournaments are not registered in the same place:

Local and divisional events are registered through AskFRED: https://www.askfred.net
Regional and national events are registered through USA Fencing's membership system: https://member.usafencing.org/search/tournaments/national

These steps are based on a project-prepared summary of official sources, not a USA Fencing-approved document. For more details, see "How do I register for a USA Fencing Tournament?" at https://usafencing.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/13085696260749-How-do-I-register-for-a-USA-Fencing-Tournament (source date: 2025-05-09).

Would you like to know how to find a specific tournament or need help with another step?

results.manualReview: Correct broad platform distinction, but national deep link used for combined regional/national guidance. Registration-only navigation refinement/retest required.

results.question: Regional registration is blocked. What can I check?

messages.text:
Regional fencing tournament registration may be blocked for several common reasons:

Membership Level: Regional events require a Competitive membership or International Competitive License. Access membership is not enough.
Age Verification: Your age must be verified in the USA Fencing membership portal before you can register.
Event Age Eligibility: You must meet the specific age requirements for the event.

If you have checked these and still cannot register, contact regionalevents@usafencing.org or the event organizer. Include the tournament name, event, your name, and membership identifier.

References:

"Why can't I register for a Regional Tournament?" (https://usafencing.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/29044338279565-Why-can-t-I-register-for-a-Regional-Tournament, updated 2024-08-06)
"How do I register for a USA Fencing Tournament?" (https://usafencing.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/13085696260749-How-do-I-register-for-a-USA-Fencing-Tournament, updated 2025-05-09)

results.question: How do I report a FenceSafe concern without sharing details here?

messages.text:
You do not need to share any details in this chat to report a FenceSafe concern. The official route is to use the USA Fencing reporting page: https://www.usafencing.org/fencesafe-report

You can submit concerns about suspected FenceSafe, conduct-code, or other policy violations there.
Anonymous reporting is possible, but it may limit follow-up.
This process is managed by USA Fencing, not by this AI or chat.

Source: "How do I report a FenceSafe Concern?" https://usafencing.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/13464818533133-How-do-I-report-a-FenceSafe-Concern (USA Fencing, 2025-05-09; project-prepared summary, not an official endorsement).
